2. `eeg-ausschreibung-freiflaeche` (Investieren & Projektbörse) – EEG-Ausschreibung Freifläche verstehen: erstes Segment (Freiflächen, Gebotstermine 1.3./1.7./1.12. – prüfen), Höchstwert 2025/2026, aktuelle Zuschlagswerte (Bundesnetzagentur, letzte Runden 2025/2026 recherchieren; ERLOESE.eegFreiflaecheCt als Orientierung), Flächenkulisse § 37 EEG (Randstreifen 500 m, Konversion, benachteiligte Gebiete + Länderöffnungsklausel), Sicherheiten (Erstsicherheit/Zweitsicherheit), Realisierungsfristen, Pönalen, Marktprämie/anzulegender Wert, § 51 negative Preise, besondere Solaranlagen, Alternativen (PPA, Merchant), Zusammenspiel. B. Große Tabelle Bundesländer. Tool → `/rechner/solarcarport`.

- operations:capacity-plan: Plan resource capacity — workload analysis and utilization forecasting. Use when heading into quarterly planning, the team feels overallocated and you need the numbers, deciding whether to hire or deprioritize, or stress-testing whether upcoming projects fit the people you have.
- operations:change-request: Create a change management request with impact analysis and rollback plan. Use when proposing a system or process change that needs approval, preparing a change record for CAB review, documenting risk and rollback steps before a deployment, or planning stakeholder communications for a rollout.
- operations:compliance-tracking: Track compliance requirements and audit readiness. Trigger with "compliance", "audit prep", "SOC 2", "ISO 27001", "GDPR", "regulatory requirement", or when the user needs help tracking, preparing for, or documenting compliance activities.
- operations:process-doc: Document a business process — flowcharts, RACI, and SOPs. Use when formalizing a process that lives in someone's head, building a RACI to clarify who owns what, writing an SOP for a handoff or audit, or capturing the exceptions and edge cases of how work actually gets done.
- operations:process-optimization: Analyze and improve business processes. Trigger with "this process is slow", "how can we improve", "streamline this workflow", "too many steps", "bottleneck", or when the user describes an inefficient process they want to fix.
- operations:risk-assessment: Identify, assess, and mitigate operational risks. Trigger with "what are the risks", "risk assessment", "risk register", "what could go wrong", or when the user is evaluating risks associated with a project, vendor, process, or decision.
- operations:runbook: Create or update an operational runbook for a recurring task or procedure. Use when documenting a task that on-call or ops needs to run repeatably, turning tribal knowledge into exact step-by-step commands, adding troubleshooting and rollback steps to an existing procedure, or writing escalation paths for when things go wrong.
- operations:status-report: Generate a status report with KPIs, risks, and action items. Use when writing a weekly or monthly update for leadership, summarizing project health with green/yellow/red status, surfacing risks and decisions that need stakeholder attention, or turning a pile of project tracker activity into a readable narrative.
- operations:vendor-review: Evaluate a vendor — cost analysis, risk assessment, and recommendation. Use when reviewing a new vendor proposal, deciding whether to renew or replace a contract, comparing two vendors side-by-side, or building a TCO breakdown and negotiation points before procurement sign-off.
- design:accessibility-review: Run a WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility audit on a design or page. Trigger with "audit accessibility", "check a11y", "is this accessible?", or when reviewing a design for color contrast, keyboard navigation, touch target size, or screen reader behavior before handoff.
- design:design-critique: Get structured design feedback on usability, hierarchy, and consistency. Trigger with "review this design", "critique this mockup", "what do you think of this screen?", or when sharing a Figma link or screenshot for feedback at any stage from exploration to final polish.
- design:design-handoff: Generate developer handoff specs from a design. Use when a design is ready for engineering and needs a spec sheet covering layout, design tokens, component props, interaction states, responsive breakpoints, edge cases, and animation details.
- design:design-system: Audit, document, or extend your design system. Use when checking for naming inconsistencies or hardcoded values across components, writing documentation for a component's variants, states, and accessibility notes, or designing a new pattern that fits the existing system.
- design:research-synthesis: Synthesize user research into themes, insights, and recommendations. Use when you have interview transcripts, survey results, usability test notes, support tickets, or NPS responses that need to be distilled into patterns, user segments, and prioritized next steps.
- design:user-research: Plan, conduct, and synthesize user research. Trigger with "user research plan", "interview guide", "usability test", "survey design", "research questions", or when the user needs help with any aspect of understanding their users through research.
- design:ux-copy: Write or review UX copy — microcopy, error messages, empty states, CTAs. Trigger with "write copy for", "what should this button say?", "review this error message", or when naming a CTA, wording a confirmation dialog, filling an empty state, or writing onboarding text.
- engineering:architecture: Create or evaluate an architecture decision record (ADR). Use when choosing between technologies (e.g., Kafka vs SQS), documenting a design decision with trade-offs and consequences, reviewing a system design proposal, or designing a new component from requirements and constraints.
- engineering:code-review: Review code changes for security, performance, and correctness. Trigger with a PR URL or diff, "review this before I merge", "is this code safe?", or when checking a change for N+1 queries, injection risks, missing edge cases, or error handling gaps.
- engineering:debug: Structured debugging session — reproduce, isolate, diagnose, and fix. Trigger with an error message or stack trace, "this works in staging but not prod", "something broke after the deploy", or when behavior diverges from expected and the cause isn't obvious.
- engineering:deploy-checklist: Pre-deployment verification checklist. Use when about to ship a release, deploying a change with database migrations or feature flags, verifying CI status and approvals before going to production, or documenting rollback triggers ahead of time.

- engineering:incident-response: Run an incident response workflow — triage, communicate, and write postmortem. Trigger with "we have an incident", "production is down", an alert that needs severity assessment, a status update mid-incident, or when writing a blameless postmortem after resolution.

# CLAUDE.md – ÖKOVOLT NetOps

Projektanweisung für Claude Code. Vor jeder Arbeit vollständig lesen.
Fachkonzept: https://claude.ai/artifact/PaFDHFySgCJKyP4yut5NGP

## 1. Projekt

Zentrale Plattform für Netzwerkdokumentation, Betrieb und Cybersicherheit der ÖKOVOLT-Gruppe.
Führendes System (Single Source of Truth für das Soll). Angebundene Systeme liefern das Ist.

**Architekturentscheidung (verbindlich):** Kein NetBox, kein IT Glue, kein Hudu.
Die App bildet DCIM, IPAM und strukturierte Dokumentation vollständig selbst ab.
Das Datenmodell orientiert sich an NetBox, damit Import/Export (NetBox-kompatibles JSON/CSV) möglich bleibt.

## 2. Stack

- Frappe Framework v15, MariaDB, Redis, Frappe Realtime (Socket.IO)
- Frontend: Vue 3 + Vite + frappe-ui, eigene SPA unter `/netops`, Leitstand unter `/screen1`–`/screen10`
- Topologie: Cytoscape.js oder Vue Flow
- Zeitreihen/Logs später: ClickHouse (nicht in MariaDB)
- Python ≥ 3.11, Node ≥ 20
- App-Name: `netops`

## 3. Konventionen

- DocType- und Feldnamen intern **englisch** (`network_device`, `ip_address`), Labels und UI **deutsch** über Übersetzungen.
- Jeder DocType: `tenant` (Link Mandant), `status`, `description`, Änderungsverfolgung an (`track_changes`).
- Beziehungen über Link/Dynamic Link, nie über Freitext.
- Keine Geschäftslogik im Frontend; Prüfungen serverseitig (Controller, Validierungen).
- Whitelisted API-Methoden nur mit expliziter Rechteprüfung (`frappe.has_permission`), nie `allow_guest`, außer der Screen-Warteseite (siehe 7).
- Tests: `bench run-tests --app netops` muss grün sein, bevor eine Aufgabe als erledigt gilt.
- Commits klein, deutschsprachige Commit-Messages, ein Thema pro Commit.

## 4. Datenmodell Phase 1 (DocTypes)

**Organisation**
- `Tenant` (Mandant): Gesellschaft, Land, Domain(s)
- `Site` (Baum): Standort → Gebäude → Raum; Adresse, Grundriss (Attach)
- `Contact`-Nutzung von Frappe; `Provider`, `Supplier`-Verweis

**DCIM**
- `Manufacturer`, `Device Type` (Hersteller, Modell, HE, Kind-Tabellen: Interface-/Power-/Front-/Rear-Port-Vorlagen)
- `Device Role`
- `Rack`: Site, Höhe in HE, Nummerierung, max. Gewicht/Last
- `Network Device`: Typ, Rolle, Site, Rack, Position/Seite, Seriennummer, Asset-Nr., Firmware, Garantie-/Support-Ende, Management-IP, Verantwortlicher (User), Lebenszyklus-Status, Passbolt-Referenz (nur ID/URL)
- `Device Interface`: Gerät, Name, Typ, MAC, Speed, Modus (access/tagged/tagged-all), Untagged-VLAN, Tagged-VLANs (Kind-Tabelle), LAG-Parent, PoE, aktiv
- `Front Port`, `Rear Port` (Patchfelder), `Power Port`, `Power Outlet`, `Power Feed`
- `Cable`: A-Ende und B-Ende (Dynamic Link auf Interface/Front Port/Rear Port/Power Port/Outlet/Wall Outlet), Typ, Farbe, Länge, Label, Status
- `Wall Outlet` (Dose): Raum, Bezeichnung
- Kabel-Trace als serverseitige Methode (`trace_path(endpoint)`)

**IPAM**
- `VRF`, `Security Zone`, `VLAN Group`, `VLAN` (VID, Name, Zone, Zweck)
- `IP Prefix` (Baum über Parent-Berechnung): Präfix, VRF, VLAN, Rolle, Site, Auslastung (berechnet)
- `IP Range` (DHCP/Pools), `IP Address`: Adresse/Maske, VRF, zugewiesenes Interface (Dynamic Link), DNS-Name, Rolle, Status
- Validierung: keine Dubletten je VRF, IP muss in einem Präfix liegen (Warnung, nicht Fehler)

**Dokumentation (IT-Glue/Hudu-Umfang)**
- `NetOps Document`: Typ (Netzplan, SOP, Runbook, Notfallplan, Wartungsprotokoll, Konfigurationsstand), Inhalt (Text Editor), Anhänge, Version, Freigabestatus
- `Object Relation`: Von (Dynamic Link) → Nach (Dynamic Link), Beziehungstyp (hängt ab von, läuft auf, dokumentiert, ersetzt …)
- `Checklist Template` + `Checklist Run` (Punkte abhaken, Pflichtpunkte, Nachweis)
- `Contract` (Laufzeit, Kündigungsfrist, Kosten, verknüpfte Objekte), `License`
- `Access Reference`: nur Verweis auf Passbolt-Eintrag (ID, URL, Bezeichnung) – **niemals Geheimnisse**

**Betrieb/Audit**
- `Audit Entry` (append-only): Zeit, Benutzer, Aktion, Objekt, Payload-Hash, `prev_hash`, `entry_hash` (SHA-256 über prev_hash + Inhalt). Kein Update/Delete (Controller verbietet es).
- `Connector`, `Connector Run`, `Raw Snapshot` (Rohdaten + Hash), `Drift Finding` (Soll/Ist-Abweichung, Status: offen/übernommen/verworfen)

## 5. Konnektor-Vertrag

Jeder Konnektor ist eine Klasse unter `netops/connectors/<name>.py`:

```python
class Connector:
    def health(self) -> dict: ...
    def pull(self) -> dict: ...                # Rohdaten, unverändert
    def normalize(self, raw: dict) -> list: ...# normierte Objekte
    # apply(change) existiert in Phase 1 NICHT
```

- Rohdaten immer als `Raw Snapshot` speichern (mit SHA-256), dann normalisieren.
- Normalisierte Objekte **nie direkt** ins Soll schreiben: Unterschiede erzeugen `Drift Finding`.
- Zugangsdaten nur über `netops.secrets.get(name)` – Phase 1 liest aus Umgebungsvariablen/`site_config` (Platzhalter), später OpenBao. Keine Tokens im Code, in DocTypes oder Logs.
- Timeouts, Retry mit Backoff, TLS-Prüfung an (eigene CA konfigurierbar, `verify=False` verboten).

**MVP-Konnektoren (nur lesen):** OPNsense, Proxmox VE, Proxmox Backup Server.

## 6. Sicherheitsregeln (nicht verhandelbar)

1. Entwicklung nur auf Test-Bench, keine Produktivdaten.
2. Nur Lese-Tokens. **Nie** Schreibzugriff auf die Perimeter-Firewall FW-OS-01 – weder im Code noch in Tests.
3. PBS-Token ohne Lösch-/Prune-Rechte.
4. Keine Geheimnisse in Repo, DocTypes, Logs, Fehlermeldungen oder Tests. `.env` in `.gitignore`.
5. Keine Befehle ausführen, die Konfigurationen an Firewalls, Switches, Hypervisor oder Backup ändern.
6. Keine Scans (nmap o. Ä.) im Netz ohne ausdrückliche Anweisung von Benny – eigene Scans müssen beim Wachhund angemeldet werden.
7. Abhängigkeiten nur aus offiziellen Quellen, `pip-audit`/`npm audit` vor jedem Merge.
8. Bei Unklarheit zu Rechten oder Zugriffen: anhalten und fragen.

## 7. MVP-Umfang (erste Sessions)

1. App `netops` anlegen, DocTypes Phase 1, Rollen: `NetOps Leser`, `NetOps Techniker`, `NetOps Security`, `NetOps Freigeber`, `NetOps Admin`, `Leitstand Anzeige`.
2. Audit-Hash-Kette inkl. Prüfmethode `verify_chain()` und Test.
3. Vue-SPA: Layout (Seitenleiste wie Mockup), globale Suche Strg+K (IP, MAC, Hostname, Seriennummer, Label, VLAN, Dose), Geräteliste, Gerätedetail mit Tabs, IPAM-Baum mit Auslastung.
4. Konnektoren OPNsense, Proxmox VE, PBS + Scheduler + Drift-Ansicht.
5. Backup-Ampel je VM/Dienst aus PBS (letztes Backup, Verify-Status, Alter).
6. **Leitstand `/screen1`** mit Freigabe-Ablauf:
   - Aufruf ohne Freigabe → Warteseite mit Bestätigungscode (6–8 Zeichen, 5 Min gültig), keine Daten.
   - Anfrage nur aus konfigurierten Leitstand-Subnetzen, sonst 403 + Audit-Eintrag.
   - `Screen Pairing Request` in der App, Freigabe durch Rolle `NetOps Admin` (Step-up-Hook vorsehen, FIDO2 folgt mit privacyIDEA).
   - Nach Freigabe: gerätegebundenes Token als HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict-Cookie, **nie** in der URL; nur Lesen, nur zugewiesener Screen.
   - Widerruf wirkt sofort (Realtime-Event), Herzschlag je Screen, veraltete Daten sichtbar markieren.
7. Offline-Export (JSON + CSV aller Kern-DocTypes) als Befehl `bench --site <site> netops-export`.

## 8. Fertig heißt

- Tests grün, keine offenen `pip-audit`/`npm audit`-Funde mit hoher Kritikalität.
- Jeder Konnektor läuft gegen die echte Testumgebung durch, `health()` grün.
- Audit-Kette verifiziert.
- Kurze Änderungsnotiz in `CHANGELOG.md`.

Claude publishes it, as an Artifact or through a first-party document connector when one is attached, and gives the person the link, so they have a private page ready to share when they choose. **To update an artifact from an earlier conversation**, Claude passes that artifact's URL as `url`. asset_ids.description: publish with `asset: true` and `from_url` only: 1–10 distinct asset ids from the source artifact (from a `scope: "assets"` listing of it, or an upload result).

favicon.description: Deprecated; Claude omits it and uses `icon`.

icon.description: One short generic word for the artifact's browser-tab icon, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map: a plain signifier, never a product or brand name. Claude includes it on every page's first publish and omits it on a redeploy so the artifact keeps its icon, passing a new one only when the person asks.

files.description: Supporting files to publish alongside the page, as a map {"published/path": "source/path" | {from, contentType} | {artifact, path, ver?} | null}. The key is what the HTML references. The source is a path on disk, or {from, contentType} when the type cannot be inferred from the published extension. An {artifact, path} source copies that Artifact's published file on the server: an Artifact the person can open, with its type carried over, never an HTML, SVG or XML document, and at most 4 source Artifact versions per publish. null removes that path on an update, and files left out are kept. A plain list publishes each file at its own spelling. Sources must be under the working directory or Claude's scratchpad directory. `preflight.js` at the artifact root is reserved: it runs against open pages when Claude publishes updates, and it must be a JavaScript module of at most 8 KiB whose default export is a function, or the publish is refused.

path.description: Path relative to the working directory (or to `root`, which may be a folder in your scratchpad directory); the file is served at this same path next to the page.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the extension for common types (css/js/json/png/…) — pass explicitly otherwise.

from.description: Source file path — relative to `root` (default: the working directory), or absolute under the working directory or your scratchpad directory.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the PUBLISHED extension for common types — pass explicitly otherwise.

artifact.description: Another artifact's claude.ai URL: the file is copied from ITS published files, server side — nothing is downloaded. You must be able to open that artifact.

path.description: The file's published path inside that Artifact, as a listing of its files prints it (not "index.html").

ver.description: A version of that Artifact to copy from instead of its current one — only versions you are served (its history, if you can edit it); omit for the current version.

root.description: The base directory that relative `files` sources resolve against, like a bundler root. It never changes published paths. It is relative to the working directory, or absolute within it or within Claude's scratchpad directory. It requires `files`.

pin.description: publish only: true also pins the published artifact to the person's claude.ai sidebar once it is published. Claude passes it only when the person asked for that. A failed pin never fails the publish, and the result says so.

limit.description: list only: the maximum number of artifacts to return (default 25).

scope.description: list: which listing to return. 'mine' is the default. The others are 'shared', 'all', 'files' (with `url`) and 'assets' (with `url`, continued with `after`). See **Calls**.

title.description: publish: the fallback title for an HTML page whose file has no <title>. It is a name, not a summary, and Claude keeps it the same across redeploys.

description.description: publish: one sentence for the subtitle on the gallery card.

label.description: A short name for this publish, at most 60 characters (e.g. "Draft to legal"). Optional. It is a few words, not a description.

overwrite_unread.description: publish with `files` or `root` to an existing artifact: published paths this call may replace or remove although you have not read or listed them in this session. Every other path the call touches must be one you read by its `path`, saw in a file listing, or published yourself, and must not have changed since — otherwise nothing is sent and the refusal names each path. Name a path here only when the user asked for it to be replaced without looking at what is there; it never excuses a path that changed after you read it.

url.description: An existing artifact's claude.ai link (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}); a chat, project or session link is not one, and `action: "list"` lists the person's artifacts. On a publish, it is the artifact to update in place, one the person owns or was given edit access to (a read of it says "writer"). Before publishing to an artifact this conversation has neither read nor published, Claude reads it (`action: "read"`) and builds on what comes back; a publish sent without that read is refused. A refusal that hands Claude the live version counts as that read: Claude merges its changes into that version and publishes the result, and never resends the refused content unchanged. Claude omits `url` for a new artifact or to redeploy a file this conversation already published. For read, delete and the other calls that take a URL, it is the artifact to act on.

prompt.description: read, for an artifact shared with the person: what Claude needs from it, which steers the isolated summary.

force.description: publish: a last-resort overwrite that **discards** the newer published version. On a conflict, Claude merges its changes onto the newer content that the rejection hands it and publishes again. Claude passes true only when the person explicitly said to discard that specific version, and the server may still refuse it over a version saved from inside the page.

out_dir.description: read with `path`: the directory to save into. The default is this artifact's folder in Claude's scratchpad directory, where saving needs no approval. A published file lands at <out_dir>/<published path>, and saving it outside that default folder asks the person first. An asset's file is named by its id plus its type's extension; saving it outside the default folder is an ordinary file save the person may be asked to approve.

path.description: read: the file's published path inside the artifact, exactly as a 'files' listing printed it ("index.html" is the page itself). The file is saved locally, the result says where, and a small text file's contents are included. It can instead be an uploaded asset's id (32 hex characters, from an 'assets' listing or an upload result), and that asset is saved to a local file. delete: the id of the one asset to remove.

paths.description: read: several published paths in place of `path`, up to 256 in one call. Each file is saved as a single `path` would be, and the result lists where each one landed, or why it could not be read, with small text files' contents included while they fit.

after.description: list with scope 'assets' only: the `next` value from a previous listing, passed to continue it.

capabilities.description: publish: the runtime capabilities this page declares, as {name: config}. Claude loads the `artifact-capabilities` skill before passing it. On a redeploy Claude omits the field to keep what the page has, and {} clears it.

contract.description: publish: the artifact's runtime version. Leaving it out keeps the current version (the default), 'latest' upgrades, and an exact version pins or rolls back. It changes how the published page behaves, so Claude passes it only when the author explicitly intends that change.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

This tool runs Git Bash (POSIX sh), not cmd.exe or PowerShell. Use Unix shell syntax: `/dev/null` not `NUL`, forward slashes, `$VAR` not `%VAR%` or `$env:VAR`. Do not use PowerShell here-strings (`@'…'@`) or backtick continuation here — for multi-line strings use a heredoc.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

schema.name: Edit
schema.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

schema.name: Glob
schema.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

schema.name: Grep
schema.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice.

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

Deliver your final report to the agent that spawned you (your caller). Use it once, for that hand-off only: when your work is complete, call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}) as your last tool call and then stop. ## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md

## claude.ai Microsoft Learn
# Microsoft Learn MCP Server

This server gives structured access to official Microsoft and Azure documentation via three tools:

## Tools

### microsoft_docs_search
Search official documentation and return up to 10 concise, high-quality content chunks (max 500 tokens each), including title, URL, and excerpt.

- Use first to get a quick, reliable overview
- Ideal for grounding answers in Microsoft knowledge

### microsoft_code_sample_search
Search for code snippets and examples in official Microsoft Learn documentation and return up to 20 relevant, high-quality code samples.

- Use when you need to provide sample Microsoft/Azure related code in your answers.  
- Ideal for generating code snippets or practical implementation examples.  
- Optional parameter `language` can filter results. 

### microsoft_docs_fetch
Fetch and convert full Microsoft documentation pages to markdown.

- Use after search when you need full content from a specific URL
- Required for detailed tutorials, troubleshooting, prerequisites, code samples, or when search results are incomplete or outdated

## Workflow

1. Use `microsoft_docs_search` to find relevant documents.
2. If you need code examples or practical snippets, use `microsoft_code_sample_search`.
3. If deeper or complete information is needed, use `microsoft_docs_fetch`.

**Search gives breadth. Code Sample Search gives practical examples. Fetch gives depth.**

All content comes from Microsoft Learn or official sources, returned in clean markdown format.

## claude.ai tldraw
Use `search` to query the tldraw Editor API spec (e.g. search for methods by category or name). Use `exec` to run JavaScript on the canvas — your code receives `editor` (the tldraw Editor instance) and helpers like toRichText, createShapeId, createArrowBetweenShapes. The current canvas state is kept in model context as raw TLShape, asset, and binding data.

## plugin:small-business:gmail
This is an MCP server provided by Gmail API. The server provides tools for developers to build LLM applications on top of Gmail.

## plugin:small-business:shopify
This server helps users set up and manage their Shopify stores.

## Store Creation
Users who don't have a store yet can use get-new-store-previews to create one from a short description.
After calling get-new-store-previews, encourage the user to browse the previews and pick the theme they like best.
Each preview has a signup link — signing up through it creates a real Shopify store with that theme and matching products pre-installed.
Encourage continued brainstorming: users can try different descriptions, tweak ideas, or explore new directions without commitment.

## Store Management
Once a store exists, this server provides tools for managing it:
- Products: search, create, update, bulk-update status, and organize into collections.
- Collections: search, create, update, and manage product groupings.
- Orders: list recent orders and get detailed order information.
- Customers: list and search customers.
- Inventory: check inventory levels and set quantities at specific locations.
- Analytics: run ShopifyQL queries for sales, order, and product performance data.
- Discounts: create percentage-based discount codes.

## GraphQL — General-Purpose Access
The Shopify Admin API exposes hundreds of resources. The built-in tools above are optimized shortcuts for common operations (with structured output and widgets), but they only cover a subset of the API.
When the user asks about a resource that has no dedicated built-in tool — such as gift cards, metafields, metaobjects, pages, blogs, markets, translations, publications, and many others — fulfill the request with the GraphQL Workflow below. NEVER tell the user that data is unavailable just because there is no built-in tool for it.

Decision logic:
1. If a built-in tool matches the request, prefer it (better UX).
2. If no built-in tool matches, run the GraphQL Workflow below. Do NOT open with graphql_query or graphql_mutation — the workflow starts at graphql_schema.

Beteiligungen: GFL – PV-Kraftwerk GmbH (100 %), HIL PV Kraftwerk GmbH (50 %, mit Prime Energy Solutions GmbH). Die Gruppe betreibt eigene Solarparks seit 2012 (z. B. Irsingen, Artern, Tilleda) und hat eigene Rammtechnik (Deutsche Solar & Rammtechnik GmbH).
- Geschäft: Projektentwicklung **Freiflächen-PV, Agri-PV, Solarcarports/Parkplätze, Großspeicher**; Contracting & PPA. Entwickelt **rund 50 MWp pro Jahr neu** (Baureife erst Jahre später – ehrlich kommunizieren).

    { id: "preise", titel: "H2 als Frage oder klare Aussage", tocLabel: "kurz fürs Inhaltsverzeichnis (optional)", bloecke: [ /* siehe Blocktypen */ ] },

};

export default artikel;

### Kategorien (feste Werte)

Belegt sind: Fachbetrieb in Türkheim, über 15 Jahre Erfahrung, Planung/Montage/Anmeldung aus einer Hand, Partner von Sigenergy, Fronius, Huawei, Solis, meteocontrol und BYD (Freigabe für deren Marketing- und Produktfotos; Bildquellen in `public/Images/Ratgeber/QUELLEN.md` dokumentieren).

# § 35 Abs. 1 Nr. 8 und 9 BauGB - Solaranlagen

## Nummer 8 (Korridor entlang Infrastruktur):
"auf einer Fläche längs von Autobahnen oder Schienenwegen des übergeordneten Netzes... und in einer Entfernung zu diesen von bis zu **200 Metern**, gemessen vom äußeren Rand der Fahrbahn"

## Nächster Termin
Die folgende Ausschreibungsrunde für PV-Freiflächenanlagen findet am **1. Dezember 2026** statt.

**Hinweis**: Das Dokument enthält keine spezifischen Informationen zu Flächenarten (Acker/benachteiligte Gebiete, Konversion, Randstreifen) oder Gesetzesänderungen.

# Zusammenfassung: Ausschreibungsverfahren Solaranlagen (Segment 1)

**Gebotstermine:** "1. März / 1. Juli / 1. Dezember" – regelmäßig dreimal jährlich

**Sicherheiten:**
- Erste Sicherheit: 50 €/kW Gebotsmenge
- Reduziert auf 25 €/kW bei Vorlage eines beschlossenen Bebauungsplans oder Planfeststellungsnachweises
- Gebühr pro Gebot: 624 Euro

**Realisierungsfrist:** 24 Monate nach Zuschlagsbekanntgabe für Inbetriebnahme; Antrag auf Zahlungsberechtigung innerhalb 26 Monaten erforderlich

**Pönalen:** Bieter zahlen Sicherheitshöhe an Übertragungsnetzbetreiber, "soweit mehr als 5 Prozent der bezuschlagten Gebotsmenge entwertet wurde"

**Maximale Gebotsgröße:** Derzeit 20 Megawatt (50 MW ausstehend Beihilfegenehmigung)

**Zuschlagsverfahren:** "Pay as bid" – Gebote mit niedrigsten Werten erhalten Zuschlag; bei Gleichheit entscheidet geringere Leistung, notfalls Losverfahren

**Voraussetzungen:** Aufstellungsbeschluss Bebauungsplan erforderlich; mindestens 1.001 kWp Anlagengröße

# § 51 EEG 2023 - Regelung negativer Strompreise

## Kernregel
Die Bestimmung legt fest: **"Für Zeiträume, in denen der Spotmarktpreis negativ ist, verringert sich der anzulegende Wert auf null."** (Abs. 1)

## Ausnahmen nach Inbetriebnahmedatum
Die Reduktion auf Null gilt **nicht** für:

1. **Kleinanlagen unter 100 kW**: vor Ausstattung mit intelligentem Messsystem
2. **Mikroanlagen unter 2 kW**: vor Festlegung durch die Bundesnetzagentur gemäß § 85 Abs. 2 Nr. 12

## Datenmitteilungspflicht
Bei Ausfallvergütung in Monaten mit negativen Preisen muss der Betreiber dem Netzbetreiber **"die Strommenge mitteilen, die er in dem Zeitraum eingespeist hat, in dem der Spotmarktpreis ohne Unterbrechung negativ gewesen ist"** (Abs. 3). Unterlassung führt zu einer Kürzung um 5 Prozent pro betroffener Kalendertag.

**Hinweis:** Die angeforderten Details zu Unterschieden ab 25.02.2025 und § 51a sind im bereitgestellten Dokumentauszug nicht enthalten.

# § 37 EEG 2023 – Gebote für Solaranlagen des ersten Segments

## Absatz 1: Zulässige Flächenkategorien

**Nr. 1 – Sonstige bauliche Anlagen:**
"Anlagen abgegeben werden, die errichtet werden sollen auf einer sonstigen baulichen Anlage, die zu einem anderen Zweck als der Erzeugung von Strom aus solarer Strahlungsenergie errichtet worden ist"

**Nr. 2 – Flächenkategorien (a–i):**

- **(a) Versiegelte Flächen:** Bereits zum Bebauungsplanbeschluss versiegelt
- **(b) Konversionsflächen:** Vorherige wirtschaftliche, verkehrliche, wohnungsbauliche oder militärische Nutzung
- **(c) § 35 BauGB-Flächen / Randstreifen:** "bis zu **500 Metern**, gemessen vom äußeren Rand der Fahrbahn"
- **(d) Alte Bebauungspläne:** Vor dem 1. September 2003 aufgestellt
- **(e) Gewerbe-/Industriegebiete:** Vor 1. Januar 2010 ausgewiesen
- **(f) Planfeststellungsverfahren:** Für Abfallbeseitigungsanlagen
- **(g) Bundesflächen:** Immobilienaufgaben-Verwaltung nach 31. Dezember 2013
- **(h) Ackerland:** In benachteiligten Gebieten (ohne Natura 2000, Biotope, Schutzgebiete)
- **(i) Grünland:** In benachteiligten Gebieten (ohne Natura 2000, Biotope, Schutzgebiete)

**Nr. 3 – Besondere Solaranlagen (a–f):**
- **(a) Agri-PV Ackerflächen:** Mit gleichzeitigem Nutzpflanzenanbau
- **(b) Dauerkultur-Agri-PV:** Mit mehrjährigen Kulturen
- **(c) Dauergrünland-Agri-PV:** Außerhalb Natura 2000
- **(d) Parkplätze:** Ohne spezifische Einschränkungen
- **(e) Moorboden-Wiedervernässung:** Mit dauerhafter Wiedervernässung
- **(f) Künstliche/veränderte Gewässer:** Nach Wasserhaushaltsgesetz

## Absatz 2: Gebotsdokumentation
Gebote erfordern Eigenerklärungen zu Eigentumsrecht, Flächeneignung, Natura 2000-Prüfung und Biodiversitätskriterien.

## Absatz 3: Gebotsgröße
"pro Gebot eine zu installierende Leistung von **50 Megawatt** nicht überschreiten"

## Absatz 4: Sperrregelung für Ackerflächen
Gebote für Ackerflächen sind unzulässig, wenn Freiflächenanlagen mit über **80 Gigawatt** installierter Leistung (nach 31. Dezember 2022) betrieben werden. Ab 1. Januar 2031 gilt eine Schwelle von **177,5 Gigawatt**.

# § 37c EEG 2023 – Regelungsinhalte

## Hauptregelung (Absatz 1)
Die Norm bestimmt, dass Gebote für Freiflächenanlagen in benachteiligten Gebieten im Ausschreibungsverfahren nicht berücksichtigt werden dürfen, sofern drei Voraussetzungen kumulativ erfüllt sind:

1. Die Landesregierung erlässt eine entsprechende Rechtsverordnung
2. Die Bundesnetzagentur wird vorher informiert
3. Eine Auslöseschwelle wird drei Monate vorher der Bundesnetzagentur mitgeteilt

## Länderöffnungsklausel (Absatz 2)
Die Regelung ermächtigt Landesregierungen zu zwei Optionen:

**Option 1 – Flächenquoten:**
- Vor 2031: Ausschluss bei mehr als 1 % landwirtschaftlicher Flächen mit Solaranlagen
- Ab 2031: Ausschluss bei mehr als 1,5 % solcher Flächen
- Länder dürfen höhere Schwellenwerte festlegen

**Option 2 – Schutzgebiete:**
Ausschluss für Anlagen auf Flächen, die zum Zeitpunkt der Bebauungsplanaufstellung bereits als „Landschaftsschutzgebiet" oder „Naturpark" festgesetzt wurden, mit Möglichkeit zusätzlicher Bedingungen.

# § 54 EEG 2023 – Zahlungsanspruchskürzungen bei Solaranlagen

## Hauptregelungen und Abschläge:

**Verspätete Realisierung (Abs. 1):**
Der ermittelte Vergütungswert sinkt um **0,3 ct/kWh**, wenn die Zahlungsberechtigung erst nach Ablauf von **18 Kalendermonaten** nach Bekanntgabe des Zuschlags beantragt wird.

**Standortabweichung (Abs. 2):**
Ein Abschlag von **0,3 ct/kWh** erfolgt, wenn der tatsächliche Anlagenstandort nicht (zumindest teilweise) mit den im Gebot angegebenen Flurstücken übereinstimmt.

**Fehlender Nutzpflanzenanbau-Nachweis (Abs. 3):**
Bei besonderen Solaranlagen mit erforderlicher gleichzeitiger Nutzpflanzenanbau- oder landwirtschaftlicher Nutzung beträgt der Abschlag **2,5 ct/kWh**, wenn dieser Nachweis gemäß Bundesnetzagentur-Festlegungen nicht erbracht wird. Der Abschlag entfällt, wenn der Nachweis nachträglich oder im Folgejahr eingereicht wird.

**Nichteinhaltung landesrechtlicher Vorgaben (Abs. 4):**
Bei Nichterfüllung erforderlicher Verordnungsvorgaben sinkt der Vergütungswert auf **null**.

# § 51a EEG 2023 - Regelung zur Vergütungszeitraum-Verlängerung

## Allgemeine Regel (Absatz 1)
Die Norm regelt, dass der Vergütungszeitraum für Strom aus Anlagen verlängert wird, wenn der anzulegende Wert auf null sinkt. Die Verlängerung entspricht der Anzahl der Viertelstunden, in denen dies im ersten Jahr und den folgenden 19 Jahren auftritt. Diese Anzahl wird auf den nächsten vollen Kalendertag aufgerundet.

## Besonderheit für Solaranlagen (Absatz 2)
Für Solaranlagen gilt eine abweichende Berechnung: „die Anzahl der Viertelstunden, um die sich der Vergütungszeitraum nach Absatz 1 Satz 1 verlängern würde, mit dem Faktor 0,5 multipliziert" wird.

Die Verlängerung erfolgt dabei nach einem Zeitkontingent-System mit monatlich differenzierten Volllastviertelstunden (z.B. 87 für Januar, 508 für Juni). Der Vergütungszeitraum verlängert sich, bis das errechnete Zeitkontingent aufgebraucht ist.

## Informationspflichten (Absätze 3-4)
Strombörsen und Übertragungsnetzbetreiber müssen bis zu festgelegten Terminen Daten über Nullpreisphasen veröffentlichen.

# Besondere Solaranlagen: Overview

Based on the Bundesnetzagentur website content provided, here's what I can confirm:

## What They Are
"Besondere Solaranlagen" (special solar installations) are solar facilities on agricultural or other specific land types, including cropland with simultaneous crop cultivation, grassland with continued agricultural use, parking areas, and rewetted moorland.

## Current Subsegment Status
The page does **not specify** a dedicated subsegment with a 9.5 ct/kWh ceiling or details about bonuses for elevated agri-PV systems. Such technical specifications are absent from this content.

## Regulatory Framework
Two key determinations govern requirements:
- **Regulation Az. 8175-07-00-21/1** (October 1, 2021) covers cropland, perennial culture areas, and parking facilities
- **Regulation Az. 4.08.01.01/1#4** addresses grassland and rewetted moorland

## Missing Information
The document does not address:
- State-aid approval status
- Current bidding mechanics
- Specific premium structures
- Page update date

For current subsidy details and state-aid confirmation, you'd need to contact the Bundesnetzagentur directly or consult more recent regulatory announcements.

# German Solar Auction Results: March 1, 2026

The Bundesnetzagentur (Federal Network Agency) announced results from a solar energy auction held on March 1, 2026, for photovoltaic ground-mounted installations and solar arrays on non-building structures.

## Key Findings

**Oversubscription:** The auction was significantly oversubscribed, with bids submitted for approximately double the available capacity. The agency stated: "Es wurden Gebote für gut das Doppelte des Ausschreibungsvolumens eingereicht" (bids were received for roughly twice the tender volume).

**Volume & Awards:** Of 532 total bids totaling 4,622 megawatts (MW) submitted for the 2,295 MW available, 268 bids received approval, totaling 2,299 MW. Thirty-nine bids were excluded.

**Pricing:** Winning bid prices ranged from 3.99 to 5.10 cents per kilowatt-hour, with the volume-weighted average at 4.94 ct/kWh—slightly lower than the previous round's 5.00 ct/kWh.

**Geographic Distribution:** Bavaria dominated with 693 MW across 106 awards, followed by Lower Saxony (340 MW) and Baden-Württemberg (333 MW).

**Project Types:** Highway and railway corridor projects led with 1,026 MW, while dual-use solar installations—which combine energy production with other land uses like agriculture—achieved record participation at 439 MW.

The next auction round is scheduled for July 1, 2026.

## Schwellenwerte für Parkplätze nach Bundesland

Die Schwellen für Parkplätze liegen je nach Bundesland zwischen 35 und 70 Stellplätzen. Hier die spezifischen Regelungen:

**Bundesländer mit Solarpflicht für Parkplätze:**

- Baden-Württemberg: offene Parkplätze mit mehr als 35 Stellplätzen
- Schleswig-Holstein: Schwelle wurde mit der Novelle von 100 auf 70 Stellplätze gesenkt
- Hessen: neue Parkplätze mit mehr als 50 Stellplätzen
- Saarland: neue Parkplätze mit mehr als 35 Stellplätzen (seit 1. September 2025)
- Bayern: offene Parkplätze oder Parkdecks mit mehr als 25 Stellplätzen
- Nordrhein-Westfalen: Parkplätze mit mehr als 35 Stellplätzen (seit 1.1.2024)
- Rheinland-Pfalz: Parkhäuser mit mehr als 50 Stellplätzen

**Bundesländer ohne Solarpflicht für Parkplätze:**

In Bayern, Berlin, Bremen, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, im Saarland, in Sachsen, Sachsen-Anhalt und Thüringen gibt es keine Solarpflicht für Parkplätze. (Anmerkung: Bei Bayern gibt es jedoch eine Ausnahme für gewerbliche Parkplätze mit mehr als 25 Stellplätzen gemäß der Bauordnung).

# Solar Obligation for Parking Lots by German State

**Article Date:** 11.09.2026

## States with Solar Requirements

| State | Threshold | Effective Date | Key Details |
|-------|-----------|-----------------|------------|
| **Baden-Württemberg** | 35+ spaces | 01.01.2022 | "60 Prozent der Stellplatzfläche mit Photovoltaik-Modulen auszustatten" required; max 10° inclination |
| **Nordrhein-Westfalen** | 35+ spaces | 01.01.2022 | Applies to commercial properties; solarthermal systems qualify as alternative |
| **Rheinland-Pfalz** | 50+ spaces | 01.01.2023 | Modules can be installed on nearby building surfaces; "mindestens 60 Prozent der Stellplatzfläche" coverage |
| **Schleswig-Holstein** | 100+ spaces | 01.01.2023 | Highest threshold; solarthermal or adjacent building installation permitted |

## States Without Parking Lot Requirements

Bavaria, Berlin, Bremen, Hamburg, and Lower Saxony have solar obligations targeting residential/commercial roofs and building renovations—not parking facilities specifically.

## General Criteria Across States

New, open parking areas suitable for solar use typically must comply. Exemptions generally apply to "Parkplätze direkt entlang von Fahrbahnen von öffentlichen Straßen" (lots directly along public roadways).

## Key Regulation

Over an open parking lot or open parking deck with more than 25 parking spaces, a solar energy system for electricity generation must be installed over the parking space area according to NBauO. This represents a recent change in the regulation.

## Timeline of Changes

The regulations have evolved:
- As of January 1, 2023, there was a requirement for new parking lot areas and parking decks with more than 50 parking spaces for motor vehicles to be covered with PV modules.
- As of 2025, newly constructed open parking lots and parking decks with more than 25 parking spaces must be covered with PV. Previously, the threshold was 50 parking spaces.

## Coverage Requirements

At least 50 percent of the parking space area suitable for solar use must be equipped with a PV system.

## Additional Details

The NBauO was revised in 2024 and the new version came into force on January 1, 2025. There are exceptions, for example in cases of economic unreasonableness, technical restrictions, or when the roof area is used for solar thermal energy.

## Key Information on Parkplatz Solarpflicht (§ 5 LSolarG)

Since January 1, 2023, with the enactment of the Landessolargesetz (LSolarG), there has been a requirement for the installation of a photovoltaic system on roofs of commercial new buildings and on newly constructed canopies of new commercial parking lots with 50 or more parking spaces.

### Specific Requirements for Parking Lots (50+ Spaces)

The obligation applies to newly constructed canopies of commercial parking lots with 50 parking spaces or more. At least 60 percent of the available parking lot area must be used for photovoltaic installation.

### Extended Requirements (Public Facilities)

With an amendment to the Landessolargesetz from the middle of the Landtag, the requirement was expanded as of January 1, 2024 to also include public buildings and parking lots – even in the case of roof renovation. The solar requirement also applies to parking lots with more than 50 parking spaces that are owned by the public.

### Exceptions and Alternatives

In exceptional cases, it is possible to resort to other external and roof surfaces in the immediate spatial vicinity.

## Summary of BauO NRW § 48 Absatz 1a - Parkplatz Photovoltaik Pflicht

Since January 2022, § 48 Absatz 1a BauO NRW 2018 mandates that for the construction of a suitable open parking lot with more than 35 parking spaces for a non-residential building, a PV system must be installed.

### Key Requirements:

- **Minimum Parking Spaces**: The requirement applies to non-residential buildings with more than 35 parking spaces, such as new supermarkets or furniture stores, where the parking lot must be covered and equipped with a photovoltaic system.

- **Minimum Solar Coverage**: The minimum area of the photovoltaic system must be 30 percent of the suitable parking area for solar use.

- **Eligible Parking Spaces**: Parking spaces serving residential use are not counted in the determination.

- **Exemptions**: This obligation is waived if the parking spaces are located along traffic roads or one tree is planted per 5 parking spaces.

### Implementation Timeline:

The obligation applies to non-residential buildings for construction permits submitted from January 1, 2024 onwards.

The regulation is implemented through both the Landesbauordnung (BauO NRW) and the "Solaranlagen-Verordnung Nordrhein-Westfalen (SAN-VO NRW)," which provide detailed implementation guidelines.

### Gesetzliche Grundlage

Die Photovoltaik-Pflicht ist in Paragraf 23 des Klimaschutz- und Klimawandelanpassungsgesetzes Baden-Württemberg (KlimaG BW) festgelegt. Das Umweltministerium Baden-Württemberg wurde durch den Landesgesetzgeber ermächtigt, durch Rechtsverordnung nähere Regelungen zur Photovoltaikpflicht zu treffen. Mit der Photovoltaik-Pflicht-Verordnung wurde diese Ermächtigungsgrundlage angewendet.

Die Photovoltaik-Pflicht sieht vor, dass mindestens 60 Prozent der Stellplatzfläche überdacht werden müssen, wenn diese in Gruppen von mindestens vier Stellplätzen angeordnet ist.

# GModG und § 106: Bundesweite Solarpflicht ab 2027

## What is GModG and § 106?

The GModG (Gebäudemodernisierungsgesetz/Building Modernization Act) is Germany's renamed building energy law, effective July 28, 2026. Section 106 introduces "the first nationwide solar obligation in Germany, staged from new non-residential construction through residential building in 2030."

## Implementation of EU Building Directive

The reform implements the European Building Directive (EPBD). The new § 106 text takes effect "six months after proclamation in the legal gazette, thus end of January 2027."

## Five-Stage Solar Mandate (2027–2031)

**January 1, 2027:**
- New public buildings (no floor-size threshold)
- New non-residential buildings exceeding 250 m² usable floor area

**January 1, 2028:**
- Existing public buildings over 2,000 m²
- Existing non-residential buildings over 500 m² undergoing modifications

**January 1, 2029:**
- Existing public buildings over 750 m²

**January 1, 2030:**
- New residential buildings
- New covered parking facilities adjacent to buildings

**January 1, 2031:**
- Existing public buildings over 250 m²

## Key Exemptions

Requirements are waived where installations are "technically impossible or functionally infeasible, economically unreasonable, or violate other public-law regulations."

## Regional Variations

Hessen and Rhineland-Palatinate maintain stricter state-level requirements alongside federal law, with differences in parking-space thresholds and applicability dates.

## Saarland Solarpflicht für Parkplätze (2025)

Since September 1, 2025, Saarland has implemented a tiered solar obligation requiring 60% of net roof area to be covered with PV systems for commercial parking facilities with 35 or more parking spaces, as well as for commercial non-residential buildings.

More specifically for parking lots: The obligation in Saarland applies to 35 commercially-used parking spaces and new parking spaces of public buildings, effective since April 26, 2025, under Saarland's Building Code (Landesbauordnung) § 12a section 2 and § 12b section 1.

## Additional Context

It's worth noting that while eight German states have solar obligations for parking lots, Saarland was previously not among them - but this changed with the new legislation in 2025. Saarland is currently the leading state among German federal states with an installed capacity of 347 kilowatts per square kilometer.

## Current Status of § 32a BbgBO

## Photovoltaic Requirement for Parking Spaces (§ 16a HmbKliSchG)

With the Climate Protection Strengthening Act passed by the Hamburg Parliament on December 6, 2023, a new requirement for the installation of photovoltaic systems on parking lot facilities (§ 16a HmbKliSchG) was introduced.

# Photovoltaik-Pflicht für Parkplätze in Schleswig-Holstein (EWKG)

**Schwelle Stellplätze:** Gilt ab mehr als 70 Stellplätzen bei Neubau/Sanierung oder bei Erweiterung um mindestens 70 Plätze.

**Deckungsgrad:** Die Anlage muss über der gesamten geeigneten Stellplatzfläche installiert werden.

**Ausnahmen:** Befreiung möglich bei unangemessenem Aufwand, Unbilligkeit, Unvereinbarkeit mit Parkplatznutzung oder rechtlicher/tatsächlicher Unmöglichkeit (z.B. Feuerwehrzufahrten, regelmäßige Veranstaltungen).

# PV-Pflicht auf Parkplätzen in Hessen

**Schwellen:**
- New parking lots with more than 50 spaces
- State-owned buildings (all new construction)

**Stichtag:**
The press release from November 16, 2022 states: "Für alle landeseigenen Gebäude und für neue Parkplätze mit mehr als 50 Stellplätzen sind künftig Photovoltaik-Anlagen vorgeschrieben" (henceforth, PV systems are mandatory).

**Rechtsgrundlage:**
Amendment to the Hessian Energy Act (Hessisches Energiegesetz), adopted by the state parliament on the Wednesday of the announcement week.

**Deckung/Funding:**
The document addresses support for building modernization but does not specify funding mechanisms for the parking lot PV mandate itself.

**Ausnahmen:**
No explicit exemptions are listed in this press release for the parking lot requirement.

**Pressemitteilung Datum:** November 16, 2022 (Hessisches Ministerium für Wirtschaft, Energie, Verkehr, Wohnen und ländlichen Raum)

# PV-Pflicht für Parkplätze in Niedersachsen (§ 32a NBauO)

**Schwelle:** Parkplätze oder Parkdecks mit **mehr als 50 Einstellplätzen** für Kraftfahrzeuge

**Deckungsgrad:** Eine Photovoltaikanlage muss über der "für eine Solarnutzung geeigneten Einstellplatzfläche" installiert werden – essentially covering suitable parking areas.

**Stichtag:** The requirement became effective on **January 1, 2025**.

**Ausnahmen:** The mandate does not apply when:

- It conflicts with other public legal requirements
- It is technically impossible
- It is economically not justifiable
- "das Dach bereits mit solarthermischen Anlagen belegt ist" (the roof is already equipped with solar thermal systems)

**Important nuance:** Exemptions do not automatically mean complete freedom from the obligation. If only part of the parking area is unsuitable, installations must cover the suitable portions.

# § 32a NBauO - Parkplatzbestimmungen

**Relevante Regelung zu Parkplätzen (Absatz 3):**

"Wird ein offener Parkplatz oder ein offenes Parkdeck mit mehr als 25 Einstellplätzen für Kraftfahrzeuge errichtet, so ist über der Einstellplatzfläche eine Solarenergieanlage zur Stromerzeugung zu installieren."

**Gültigkeitszeitraum:**

Die aktuelle Fassung ist seit dem **1. Januar 2025** in Kraft und stellt die derzeit geltende Version dar.

**Hinweis:** Die Regelung erfordert die Installation einer Solaranlage über Parkplätze ab 26 Einstellplätzen. Eine entsprechende Verpflichtung besteht auch bei wesentlichen Änderungen oder Erneuerungen von mindestens 50 Prozent einer bestehenden Parkplatzfläche.

Based on the search results, here's what § 32a NBauO regulates regarding parking lots with more than 25 parking spaces and photovoltaic requirements:

## Photovoltaic Requirement for Large Parking Lots

When an open parking lot or an open parking deck with more than 25 parking spaces for motor vehicles is erected, a solar energy system for electricity generation must be installed above the parking space area.

## Additional Regulations

The same obligation also applies when at least 50 percent of the existing area of an open parking lot is substantially changed or renewed in its dimensions or road construction.

Exempt from these obligations are parking lots that are arranged directly along the roadways of public streets and are dedicated to public traffic.

The obligations also apply when the parking lot or parking deck is used by multiple usage units, including in different buildings.

## Recent Changes

Since 2025, newly erected open parking lots and parking decks with more than 25 parking spaces must be covered with PV systems. Previously, the threshold was 50 parking spaces.

This regulation is part of Lower Saxony's (Niedersachsen) effort to advance the expansion of emission-free energy generation through mandatory solar installations on parking infrastructure.

content.content:
# § 11 GEIG - Bestehende Nichtwohngebäude

Nach § 11 Abs. 3 GEIG gelten die Vorschriften des Gesetzes für bestehende gemischt genutzte Gebäude, die „zusammen über mehr als zehn Stellplätze innerhalb des Gebäudes oder über mehr als zehn an das Gebäude angrenzende Stellplätze verfügen".

Die angeforderte Norm betrifft bestehende Nichtwohngebäude mit einer Schwelle von **mehr als 10 Stellplätzen**. Im bereitgestellten Text ist jedoch **keine spezifische Frist für 2025** erwähnt. Die Regelung in § 11 GEIG behandelt allgemein die Anwendbarkeit des Gesetzes auf bestehende und neue gemischt genutzte Gebäude, nennt aber in dieser Bestimmung keine zeitliche Befristung.

# § 10 GEIG - Bestehende Nichtwohngebäude

**Stellplatz-Schwelle:**
"Für jedes Nichtwohngebäude, das über mehr als 20 Stellplätze innerhalb des Gebäudes oder über mehr als 20 an das Gebäude angrenzende Stellplätze verfügt" muss ein Ladepunkt errichtet werden.

**Ladepunkte-Anforderung:**
Nach dem 1. Januar 2025 ist der Eigentümer verpflichtet, mindestens einen Ladepunkt pro betroffenes Gebäude zu schaffen.

**Leitungsinfrastruktur:**
Der Text regelt die Errichtung von Ladepunkten selbst, behandelt aber keine spezifische Quote für Leitungsinfrastruktur bei bestehenden Nichtwohngebäuden.

**Flexibilisierung:**
Eigentümer mehrerer betroffener Gebäude können "die Gesamtzahl der zu errichtenden Ladepunkte zusammen in einer oder mehreren seiner Liegenschaften errichten", sofern der Bedarf angemessen berücksichtigt wird.

# PV-Pflicht auf Parkplätzen in Baden-Württemberg

**Rechtsgrundlage:**
§ 23 des Klimaschutz- und Klimawandelanpassungsgesetzes Baden-Württemberg (KlimaG BW) und die Photovoltaik-Pflicht-Verordnung (PVPf-VO).

**Geltungsschwelle & Stichtag:**
Die Pflicht greift beim "Neubau eines offenen Parkplatzes mit mehr als 35 Stellplätzen" ab dem 1. Januar 2022.

**Mindestabdeckung:**
"60 Prozent der Eignungsfläche" müssen mit Photovoltaikmodulen belegt werden. Module sind nicht über Fahrgassen erforderlich.

**Anforderungen an Flächen:**
Mindestens vier Stellplätze müssen zusammenhängend angeordnet sein, ausschließlich für Personenkraftwagen, mit maximaler Neigung von 10 Grad.

**Ausnahmen:**
Parkplätze ohne Netzanschluss oder bei Netzanschlussverweigerung sind ausgenommen.

**Ersatzerfüllung:**
Photovoltaikmodule können alternativ auf Dachflächen oder Außenflächen eines gleichzeitig neu errichteten Gebäudes in unmittelbarer räumlicher Umgebung installiert werden – jedoch nur auf Flächen, die nicht bereits der Gebäudepflicht unterliegen.

**Grundlegende Sanierung:**
Die Parkplatz-Pflicht unterscheidet sich von Gebäuden – für bestehende Parkplätze gelten keine Sanierungspflichten.

**Original Regulation (effective from 2023):**
Starting in 2023, photovoltaic systems must be installed on all commercially used new buildings with more than 100 square meters of usable space and on commercially used new parking lots with 50 or more parking spaces. **Expansion in 2024:**
Starting in 2024, the photovoltaic requirement also applies to public new buildings and parking lots in Rheinland-Pfalz. The requirements apply from January 1, 2023 for commercially used parking lots and from January 1, 2024 for parking lots of the public sector.

The 50 parking space threshold ("50 Stellplätze") and the 60 percent minimum coverage requirement you mentioned are indeed core components of § 5 of the Landessolargesetz, with the key modification in 2024 being the extension to public buildings and parking lots, not a change to the commercial threshold itself.

## Parkplatzüberdachung mit Photovoltaik

Im Kanton Bern soll bei Neubauten grosser Parkplatzanlagen und Parkdecks eine Pflicht für die Überdachung mit Photovoltaik eingeführt werden. Im Kanton Bern gelten ab 1. Januar 2026 neue Vorschriften zur Solarpflicht für Neubauten und Erweiterungen sowie für Parkplätze.

Neue Parkplätze im Freien ab 80 Abstellplätzen, die der Allgemeinheit zur Verfügung stehen und kostenpflichtig sind, sowie Park-and-Ride-Anlagen im Freien mit mehr als 50 Abstellplätzen sind mit solaraktiver Überdachung auszustatten.

## Befreiungen und Ausnahmen

Liegt die solare Einstrahlung der betroffenen Bodenfläche unter 1000 kWh/m2a, sind diese von der Solarpflicht befreit.

## Nationale Solarpflicht

Bis 2035 sollen auf Parkplätzen im ganzen Land Solarüberdachungen installiert werden. Dies gilt für Abstellflächen ab einer Mindestfläche für 21 Autos.

## Kantonale Unterschiede

Ein Nachzug auf eidgenössischer Ebene ist unwahrscheinlich, denn in Sachen Energiegesetz sind die Kantone selbst zuständig. Einige Kantone wie Luzern, Zürich und Bern haben bereits strengere oder weitergehende Solarpflichten eingeführt als der Bund vorgibt.
